scope: Two route-free official MCP SDK 2.3.1 replays against a checksum-verified unsigned experimental Debian 12 amd64 package from exact-main source 3211c1c1a587291d70647c877e036ca81c2848ca; each used a disposable 128 MiB, 64 PID container with a 64-FD server soft limit
reproduce: Download the experimental-candidate-linux-x86_64 artifact from CI run 42976396612; verify every SHA256SUMS entry; set OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_DIR=$PWD/tools/mcp-sdk-probe, OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_PACKAGE to the verified .deb, and OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_PACKAGE_SHA256 to its digest; run bash tools/netns_adversarial_probe.sh target/debug/outbound-guard-mcp twice.
checks: The independent SDK probe made 52 serial allowed calls, submitted 16 concurrent calls with eight host slots left, filled to 60 approvals and confirmed a final rate denial. Both runs returned eight allowed, one rate denial and seven input-busy results in the burst. Fixture counters required exactly 60 allowed.test A and AAAA queries and 60 /plain HTTP hits; SDK audit counts, discovery, package installation, removal, residue and container cleanup passed. The overall suite decision totals vary with a separate earlier concurrent audit phase.
limitations: Client submissions are concurrent; simultaneous server execution is not proven. No packet capture or host-client/other-tool traffic coverage. This is one experimental Debian package and SDK client, not native Codex/Claude/Cursor, multi-process budget proof, official candidate, owner acceptance, independent human review, or evidence for the four AI Scraping Defense repositories.
